questions.question: Find the bug in this script that tries to run a detached Nginx container and then list running containers.
questions.codeSnippet:
docker run -d --name web nginx
docker ps -a
docker exec web bash
questions.explanation: The command `docker exec web bash` attempts to open an interactive shell but does not allocate a pseudo‑TTY. It should be `docker exec -it web bash`. Without `-it`, the shell starts but immediately exits or hangs without a terminal.

questions.question: Identify the error in the following sequence that tries to stop and remove all containers.
questions.codeSnippet:
docker stop $(docker ps -q)
docker rm $(docker ps -q)
questions.explanation: After stopping the running containers, the second command `docker ps -q` will return an empty list because only running containers are listed by default. To remove the stopped containers, you should use `docker rm $(docker ps -aq)` to include all containers (stopped as well).

questions.question: Spot the mistake in this attempt to copy a file from a container that no longer exists.
questions.codeSnippet:
docker run --rm alpine echo hello
docker exec alpine ls
questions.explanation: The container was run with `--rm`, so it is automatically removed after `echo` exits. Therefore the second command `docker exec alpine ls` will fail because no container named `alpine` is running.

questions.question: What is wrong with this command that tries to get an interactive shell inside a stopped container?
questions.codeSnippet:
docker stop mybox
docker exec -it mybox sh
questions.explanation: `docker exec` only works on running containers. Since `mybox` was just stopped, the second command will fail. You must first start the container with `docker start mybox`.

questions.question: Find the bug in this Dockerfile that fails to build.
questions.codeSnippet:
FROM ubuntu
RUN apt-get update
COPY . /app
CMD ["python", "app.py"]
questions.explanation: The Dockerfile tries to run a Python script but never installs Python. The `RUN apt-get update` does not install Python. It should include `RUN apt-get install -y python3`.

questions.question: Identify the mistake in this command sequence when trying to remove an image.
questions.codeSnippet:
docker run --name myapp alpine echo hello
docker rmi alpine
questions.explanation: After `docker run`, the container exists but is stopped. The image `alpine` is still referenced by that stopped container. `docker rmi alpine` will fail unless you force it or remove the container first.

questions.question: What is wrong with this `docker stats` usage?
questions.codeSnippet:
docker run --rm alpine sleep 1
docker stats alpine
questions.explanation: The container was run with `--rm` and `sleep 1`, so it exits almost immediately. The `docker stats` command fails because no container named `alpine` is running.
